meta.title: Swedish B1 Intermediate
meta.subtitle: 1000 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Swedish → English (see the Swedish, recall the meaning) and English → Swedish (see an English meaning, recall the Swedish). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1000 words of Swedish for an intermediate learner, aligned to B1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand the main points of clear standard input on familiar matters regularly encountered in work, school, leisure, etc.' — a learner here is able to deal with most situations likely to arise whilst travelling, to produce simple connected text on topics which are familiar or of personal interest, and to describe experiences and events, dreams, hopes and ambitions and briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions and plans. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: Swedish has examinations at these levels — Swedex and Tisus — but neither was found to publish a word list, so this deck is not an examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 273 of the 1000 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — work and the economy, society and politics, media and technology, the environment, education, relationships and family life, home and housing, health, travel and experiences, culture and leisure, feelings and opinions, the words of explaining and arguing, the verbs and adjectives of judging, time and frequency, and the connectors that build an argument — and the other 727 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Swedish, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every form of a noun or a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. The 533 nouns are printed with their article — en or ett — because the article is the gender, which decides the noun's definite ending, the adjective's ending and the pronoun that stands for it, and they show their definite singular and their plural (bilen, bilar); the 247 verbs show their present, past and supine, the three forms a Swedish verb is learnt by (äter, åt, ätit), and behind the All forms fold their imperative, -s forms and participles. Real example sentences come with 911 of the 1000 words, three apiece for 719 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, gender and forms: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
